detail.body:
# ZeRO-3 CPU offload: apply the clip factor and write the bf16 copy inside the CPU Adam pass

<!-- r3 2026-10-15, new PR. Branch peng-add-cpu-adam-fused-step-v1 (worktree /fsx/peng/workspace/ds-add-cpu-adam-fused-step)
on master 5f266e26d. Stacked on the pinned copy-back PR (branch peng-fix-zero3-offload-pinned-copy-v2): the branch gets
that PR's commit first, then this one. Patches: pr-prep/patches/2026-10-15/zero3-offload-pinned-copy-r3.patch, then
cpu-adam-fused-step-on-pinned-copy-r3.patch (checked: the two applied to master give exactly the worktree). Evidence:
deepspeed-500b-study/latest-code-review/README.md (trees v10 / v11 / v11b; job IDs: SOURCES.md). -->

**Builds on:** #TODO(pinned copy-back PR number) (ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back through pinned buffers).
This branch contains that PR's commit followed by this one; review the second commit.
**Part of:** #8672 (Q4 2026 roadmap), "Enable training of large scale models".

## Summary

With the optimizer offloaded to the CPU, ZeRO-3's step makes three passes over every CPU sub-group:

1. multiply every fp32 gradient by the clipping factor in place (`grad.mul_`), even when the factor is 1;
2. run `DeepSpeedCPUAdam` (reads gradients, parameters and both moments; writes parameters and both moments);
3. cast the updated fp32 parameters to bf16 into the pinned staging buffers and copy them to the device.

This PR folds 1 and 3 into 2: the CPU Adam kernel multiplies each gradient by the factor as it loads it, and writes
the bf16 copy of each updated piece into a pinned staging buffer, which is copied to the device while the next piece
is updated. The parameters after training are bitwise equal to the three-pass path.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and recent pull requests on 2026-10-15 ("cpu adam", "offload", "pinned", "master weights"): no PR
fuses the clip factor or the copy-back into the CPU Adam step. Related but different: #8673 fuses mixed-precision
gradients and the parameter writeback into the GPU `FusedAdam`; #8813 builds the CPU optimizer ops without CUDA and
fixes the CPU Lion update; #8817 adds an RVV kernel to CPU Adam (both change the same C++ files, so whichever merges
later rebases); #8719 adds asynchronous CPU-offloaded optimizers.

## The change

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---|---|
| `csrc/includes/cpu_adam.h` | +72 -1 | `_grad_scale`, `_params_copy`, `set_grad_scale`, `set_params_copy`, `params_copy_for`: the step multiplies each loaded gradient by the factor and, when a copy buffer is set, stores the updated parameter in bf16 there |
| `csrc/includes/sve.h` | +4 -1 | the SVE path takes the factor |
| `csrc/adam/cpu_adam_impl.cpp` | +117 | `ds_adam_step_scaled`, `ds_adam_step_scaled_copy`, `ds_adam_copy_supported`, `ds_adam_block_numel` |
| `csrc/adam/cpu_adam.cpp` | +14 | bindings `adam_update_scaled`, `adam_update_scaled_copy`, `adam_copy_supported`, `adam_block_numel` |
| `deepspeed/ops/adam/cpu_adam.py` | +66 -4 | `step(closure=None, grad_scale=1.0)`; `copy_supported()`; `step_pieces(piece_numel, before_piece, after_piece, grad_scale=1.0)` updates a parameter piece by piece, `before_piece` returns the bf16 buffer for the piece, `after_piece` starts its copy; the piece size is rounded down to a multiple of the kernel's widest vector block (`adam_block_numel`, 128 floats with AVX512) so every element takes the vector path, as in one call on the whole tensor |
| `deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py` | +97 -10 | `_grad_scale_for_cpu_adam` passes the factor to CPU Adam instead of `mul_` for CPU sub-groups; `_cpu_adam_step_and_copy_back` runs `step_pieces` into the two pinned staging buffers of the copy-back PR, waits for the previous copy out of a buffer before refilling it, and waits for the last piece before returning (the next forward's all-gathers do not wait for this stream) |
| `tests/unit/ops/adam/test_cpu_adam.py` | +78 | kernel tests below |
| `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py` | +118 | ZeRO-3 tests below |

Where the fused path runs: CPU sub-groups with float32 gradients and master weights, `pin_memory` on, a bf16 device
partition, and a CPU Adam build with a bf16 store (AVX512, NEON and the scalar loop; `copy_supported()` asks the build).
Everything else (fp16 or a GradScaler, ZenFlow, NVMe offload, Muon, SuperOffload, `pin_memory` off) keeps the current
path. No configuration key changes.

## Measured

GLM-5.2, real weights, PG-19 rows of 65,536 tokens, fp32 Adam states, CPU optimizer offload, each sequence over 2 GPUs.

| Setup | Without this PR | With this PR | Same losses |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 node x 8 H200, first 8 layers, 20% of the optimizer on the GPU: clip factor fused | 15.95 s per step, optimizer step 5.01-5.29 s | 15.01 s, optimizer step 4.25-4.33 s | yes |
| the same, clip factor and bf16 copy fused (2 runs) | 15.95 s | 14.61-14.67 s (-8.0 to -8.4%) | yes |
| 8 nodes x 8 H200, all 78 layers, 10% on the GPU, one job on the same nodes | 147.16 s | 143.61 s (-2.4%) | yes (to the printed digits until step 8, then one bf16 step, as between repeated runs) |

Profile (one step, rank 1): the separate `aten::mul_` pass took 824 ms of a 6.70 s step on 2 nodes before;
with this PR it is 1.2 ms in an 8-node step, and no separate cast pass remains after the backward.
Memory: no new buffers (the staging buffers belong to the copy-back PR).

This change was also in the DeepSpeed tree of our MiniMax-M3 and GLM-5.2 runs against Megatron-LM (real weights,
65,536-token sequences, 80-95% of the optimizer on the CPU): MiniMax-M3 on 4 nodes 85.24 s per step vs 119.35 s for
Megatron-LM (one job on the same nodes); GLM-5.2 first 38 layers on 4 nodes 62.03 vs 63.73 s (one job on the same nodes);
GLM-5.2 all 78 layers on 8 nodes 130.58 vs 135.56 s (separate jobs on 7 of the same 8 nodes). On one node, master plus this
PR, the copy-back PR and the two model PRs (#8658, #8659) gives the same loss at every step as that tree.

## Tests

| Test | Checks |
|---|---|
| `test_cpu_adam_grad_scale_matches_scaling_in_place` | `step(grad_scale=f)` gives bitwise the parameters and moments of `grad.mul_(f)` then `step()` |
| `test_cpu_adam_step_pieces_matches_step` | `step_pieces` with pieces of 1,000 elements (not a multiple of the vector block) and 524,289-element tensors gives bitwise the result of one `step()`, and the bf16 copies equal `param.to(torch.bfloat16)` |
| `TestZero3CpuAdamGradScale` (2 ranks; clip 1e-3 and 1e6; ratio 1.0 and 0.5) | ZeRO-3 with CPU offload: parameters after 3 steps bitwise equal to the in-place path; the fused path ran; factor below 1 when clipping, 1 otherwise |
| `TestZero3CpuAdamCopyBack` (2 ranks; ratio 1.0 and 0.5) | staging pieces of 1,000 elements reuse both buffers many times per step; parameters bitwise equal to the separate passes; the fused copy-back ran |

Hardware: 1 node of 8 H200 (143,771 MiB, driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126, pytest 9.1.1:

```
pytest unit/ops/adam/test_cpu_adam.py                                  # 137 passed, 5 skipped (master: 97 passed, 5 skipped)
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestZero3CpuAdamGradScale            # 4 passed
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestZero3CpuAdamCopyBack             # 2 passed
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestZero3OffloadPinnedCopyBack       # 2 passed
pytest unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_offloadpp.py                        # 3 passed (master: 3 passed)
```

The 5 skips are the file's own fp16 cases. `pre-commit run --files` passes on every changed file.

## Compatibility

| Cell | Validated |
|---|---|
| ZeRO-3, CPU optimizer offload, `pin_memory` on, bf16, all of the optimizer on the CPU (ratio 1.0) and half (0.5) | yes (tests; 1 and 8 nodes) |
| AVX512 build (Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, the H200 nodes) | yes |
| NEON / SVE builds, AVX2-only CPUs | no (AVX2 has no bf16 store, so `copy_supported()` is false and the copy keeps the old path; the clip factor is fused on every build) |
| fp16, GradScaler, NVMe offload, ZenFlow, Muon, SuperOffload, `pin_memory` off | path unchanged by design |
| ZeRO-1 / ZeRO-2 | not touched |

## AI assistance

This change, its tests and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

         .. note::
@@ -122,6 +122,10 @@ def step(self, closure=None):
         Args:

+            grad_scale (float, optional): every gradient is multiplied by this
+                factor as the kernel loads it, the same float multiply as
+                ``grad.mul_(grad_scale)`` before the step but without a separate
+                pass over the gradients (which are left unchanged). Defaults to 1.
 
         Returns:
             loss: if ``closure`` is provided. Otherwise ``None``.
@@ -163,11 +167,69 @@ def step(self, closure=None):
                 state['step'] += 1
                 beta1, beta2 = group['betas']
 
-                self.ds_opt_adam.adam_update(self.opt_id, state['step'], group['lr'], beta1, beta2, group['eps'],
-                                             group['weight_decay'], group['bias_correction'], p.data, p.grad.data,
-                                             state['exp_avg'], state['exp_avg_sq'])
+                if grad_scale != 1.0:
+                    self.ds_opt_adam.adam_update_scaled(self.opt_id, state['step'], group['lr'], beta1, beta2,
+                                                        group['eps'], group['weight_decay'], group['bias_correction'],
+                                                        p.data, p.grad.data, state['exp_avg'], state['exp_avg_sq'],
+                                                        grad_scale)
+                else:
+                    self.ds_opt_adam.adam_update(self.opt_id, state['step'], group['lr'], beta1, beta2, group['eps'],
+                                                 group['weight_decay'], group['bias_correction'], p.data, p.grad.data,
+                                                 state['exp_avg'], state['exp_avg_sq'])
         return loss
 
+    def copy_supported(self):
+        """Whether step_pieces can write a bfloat16 copy of the updated parameters (needs AVX512, NEON or the
+        scalar kernel)."""
+        return bool(self.ds_opt_adam.adam_copy_supported())
+
+    def aligned_piece_numel(self, piece_numel):
+        """The piece size step_pieces uses for ``piece_numel``: rounded down to a multiple of the kernel's widest
+        vector block (at least one block), so every element goes through the same code, with the same rounding, as in
+        one step() call on the whole parameter."""
+        block = int(self.ds_opt_adam.adam_block_numel())
+        return max(block, piece_numel - piece_numel % block)
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def step_pieces(self, piece_numel, before_piece, after_piece, grad_scale=1.0):
+        """step(grad_scale=...) for float32 parameters, done in pieces of ``piece_numel`` elements, with a bfloat16
+        copy of each updated piece written by the same kernel pass.
+
+        Pieces are ``aligned_piece_numel(piece_numel)`` elements (the last one may be shorter).
+        For each piece of each parameter: ``out = before_piece(param, start, count)`` returns a contiguous bfloat16
+        CPU tensor of ``count`` elements; the kernel updates the piece and writes it, rounded to nearest even (as
+        ``out.copy_(param[start:start + count])`` would), into ``out``; then ``after_piece(param, start, count, out)``.
+        The parameters and moments are bitwise equal to step(grad_scale=...).
+        """
+        assert self.copy_supported(), "step_pieces needs AVX512, NEON or the scalar CPU Adam kernel"
+        piece_numel = self.aligned_piece_numel(piece_numel)
+        device = torch.device('cpu')
+        for group in self.param_groups:
+            for p in group['params']:
+                if p.grad is None:
+                    continue
+                assert p.device == device and p.dtype == torch.float32, \
+                    f"step_pieces needs float32 CPU parameters, got {p.dtype} on {p.device}"
+                state = self.state[p]
+                if len(state) == 0:
+                    state['step'] = 0
+                    state_dtype = torch.float if self.fp32_optimizer_states else p.dtype
+                    state['exp_avg'] = torch.zeros_like(p.data, dtype=state_dtype, device=device)
+                    state['exp_avg_sq'] = torch.zeros_like(p.data, dtype=state_dtype, device=device)
+                state['step'] += 1
+                beta1, beta2 = group['betas']
+                param, grad = p.data.view(-1), p.grad.data.view(-1)
+                exp_avg, exp_avg_sq = state['exp_avg'].view(-1), state['exp_avg_sq'].view(-1)
+                for start in range(0, param.numel(), piece_numel):
+                    count = min(piece_numel, param.numel() - start)
+                    out = before_piece(p, start, count)
+                    piece = slice(start, start + count)
+                    self.ds_opt_adam.adam_update_scaled_copy(self.opt_id, state['step'], group['lr'], beta1, beta2,
+                                                             group['eps'], group['weight_decay'],
+                                                             group['bias_correction'], param[piece], grad[piece],
+                                                             exp_avg[piece], exp_avg_sq[piece], grad_scale, out)
+                    after_piece(p, start, count, out)
+
     @torch.no_grad()
     def step_subgroup(self, subgroup_id: int, closure=None):
         """Update the model parameters in a single subgroup (by index)."""

@@ -251,6 +251,12 @@ def __init__(
 
         self.offload_optimizer = False
         self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory = False
+        # Pinned buffers for copying CPU master partitions back to the device (_copy_through_pinned_staging). The
+        # element count is a power of two, so the pinned allocator does not round the buffers up.
+        self._staging_numel = 2**26

+        self._staging_events = None
         self.offload_optimizer_fast_init = False

@@ -562,6 +568,8 @@ def _unpin_offload_buffers(self):
                 accelerator.unpin_memory(buffer)

         unpin_offloaded_optimizer_states(self.optimizer)
         if self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory:
             for fp32_partition in self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat:
@@ -1231,7 +1239,9 @@ def _create_fp16_sub_groups(self, params_group):
 
         return sub_groups
 
-    def _optimizer_step(self, sub_group_id):

+        loaded (the sub-group's gradients were not scaled in place); None when they were."""
         param_group_id = self.sub_group_to_group_id[sub_group_id]
         fp32_param = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id]

-                step_with_gradscaler(self.optimizer)
+                if grad_scale is not None:
+                    self.optimizer.step(grad_scale=grad_scale)
+                else:
+                    step_with_gradscaler(self.optimizer)
                 self.optimizer.param_groups[param_group_id]['params'] = []
             else:
                 self.backup_optimizer.param_groups[param_group_id]['params'] = [fp32_param]
@@ -2849,13 +2862,105 @@ def _post_step(self, timer_names):
         see_memory_usage('After zero_optimizer step', force=False)
         print_rank_0("------------------Finishing Step-----------------------")
 
+    @instrument_w_nvtx
+    def _copy_through_pinned_staging(self, dst, src):
+        """Copy the pageable CPU master partition ``src`` into the device partition ``dst`` through two small pinned
+        buffers: each piece is cast on the CPU into one buffer while the previous piece is copied from the other.
+
+        Copies from pageable memory run at a few GB/s. Pinning the master partitions themselves, as ZeRO-1/2 does,
+        would also need a pinned low-precision buffer of each partition's size, so pinned host memory would grow with
+        the model; these two buffers have a fixed size."""
+        numel = src.numel()
+        chunk = self._staging_numel
+        if self._staging_buffers is None or self._staging_buffers[0].dtype != dst.dtype:
+            self._staging_buffers = [get_accelerator().pin_empty(chunk, dtype=dst.dtype) for _ in range(2)]
+            self._staging_events = [None, None]
+        src = src.view(-1)
+        dst = dst.view(-1)
+        last_event = None
+        for index, start in enumerate(range(0, numel, chunk)):
+            buf = index % 2
+            if self._staging_events[buf] is not None:
+                # The previous copy out of this buffer must finish before the buffer is refilled.
+                self._staging_events[buf].synchronize()
+            count = min(chunk, numel - start)
+            staging = self._staging_buffers[buf][:count]
+            staging.copy_(src[start:start + count])
+            dst[start:start + count].copy_(staging, non_blocking=True)
+            event = get_accelerator().Event()
+            event.record()
+            self._staging_events[buf] = event
+            last_event = event
+        # Callers expect the partition on the device when this returns: the parameter all-gathers of the next forward
+        # run on a stream that does not wait for this one.
+        if last_event is not None:
+            last_event.synchronize()
+
+    def _can_copy_back_from_cpu_adam(self, sub_group_id):
+        """Whether _cpu_adam_step_and_copy_back can replace _optimizer_step + _reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters
+        for this CPU sub-group (called only when _grad_scale_for_cpu_adam returned a factor): the device partition is
+        bfloat16 and would be copied through the pinned staging buffers, and the CPU Adam build can write the
+        bfloat16 copy."""
+        if self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id] is None or not self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory:
+            return False
+        dst = self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id]
+        src = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id]
+        if dst.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or dst.device.type == "cpu" or src.is_pinned():
+            return False
+        if self._cpu_adam_copy_supported is None:
+            self._cpu_adam_copy_supported = self.optimizer.copy_supported()
+        return self._cpu_adam_copy_supported
+
+    def _cpu_adam_step_and_copy_back(self, sub_group_id, grad_scale):
+        """CPU Adam on this sub-group in pieces of the pinned staging size: for each piece the kernel updates the
+        fp32 parameters and writes them in bfloat16 into one staging buffer, which is copied to the device partition
+        while the next piece is updated. Replaces _optimizer_step followed by _copy_through_pinned_staging (which
+        reads the fp32 parameters again to cast them); same values, same rounding."""
+        param_group_id = self.sub_group_to_group_id[sub_group_id]
+        fp32_param = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id]
+        dst = self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data.view(-1)
+        chunk = self._staging_numel
+        if self._staging_buffers is None or self._staging_buffers[0].dtype != dst.dtype:
+            self._staging_buffers = [get_accelerator().pin_empty(chunk, dtype=dst.dtype) for _ in range(2)]
+            self._staging_events = [None, None]
+        pieces = {"index": 0, "last_event": None}
+
+        def before_piece(param, start, count):
+            buf = pieces["index"] % 2
+            if self._staging_events[buf] is not None:
+                self._staging_events[buf].synchronize()  # the previous copy out of this buffer has finished
+            return self._staging_buffers[buf][:count]
+
+        def after_piece(param, start, count, out):
+            dst[start:start + count].copy_(out, non_blocking=True)
+            event = get_accelerator().Event()
+            event.record()
+            self._staging_events[pieces["index"] % 2] = event
+            pieces["last_event"] = event
+            pieces["index"] += 1
+
+        self.optimizer.param_groups[param_group_id]['params'] = [fp32_param]
+        self.optimizer.step_pieces(chunk, before_piece, after_piece, grad_scale=grad_scale)
+        self.optimizer.param_groups[param_group_id]['params'] = []
+        # As _copy_through_pinned_staging: the data must be on the device before returning (the next forward's
+        # parameter all-gathers run on a stream that does not wait for this one).
+        if pieces["last_event"] is not None:
+            pieces["last_event"].synchronize()
+        self._unflatten_partitioned_parameters(sub_group_id)
+
     @instrument_w_nvtx
     def _reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters(self, sub_group_id):
         if self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id] is not None:
             # When torch autocast is enabled, groups in fp16_partitioned_groups are in fp32 already and those in
             # fp32_partitioned_groups are aliases. Calling tensor.data.copy_ will not trigger any copy in that case.
-            self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data.copy_(
-                self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data)
+            dst = self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data
+            src = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data
+            accelerator = get_accelerator()
+            src_is_pageable = src.device.type == "cpu" and not accelerator.is_pinned(src)
+            if self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory and src_is_pageable and dst.device.type != "cpu":
+                self._copy_through_pinned_staging(dst, src)
+            else:
+                dst.copy_(src)
 
             #unflatten fp16 parameter subgroup
             self._unflatten_partitioned_parameters(sub_group_id)
@@ -2913,14 +3018,20 @@ def step(self, closure=None):
             if self._muon_update_lacks_loss_scale(sub_group_id):
                 self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].grad.mul_(self.loss_scale)
 
-            #scale the fp32 gradients
-            self.unscale_and_clip_grads(sub_group_id, scaled_global_grad_norm)
+            #scale the fp32 gradients; DeepSpeedCPUAdam applies the factor as it loads each gradient instead
+            grad_scale = self._grad_scale_for_cpu_adam(sub_group_id, scaled_global_grad_norm)
+            if grad_scale is None:
+                self.unscale_and_clip_grads(sub_group_id, scaled_global_grad_norm)
 
-            #apply the optimizer step on the sub group and copy fp32 parameters to fp16
-            self._optimizer_step(sub_group_id)
+            if grad_scale is not None and self._can_copy_back_from_cpu_adam(sub_group_id):
+                #one kernel pass updates the fp32 parameters and writes their bf16 copy, piece by piece
+                self._cpu_adam_step_and_copy_back(sub_group_id, grad_scale)
+            else:
+                #apply the optimizer step on the sub group and copy fp32 parameters to fp16
+                self._optimizer_step(sub_group_id, grad_scale=grad_scale)
 
-            #put fp16 parameters in appropriate location
-            self._reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters(sub_group_id)
+                #put fp16 parameters in appropriate location
+                self._reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters(sub_group_id)
 
             #release memory or swap out optimizer states of fp32 parameters
             self._release_sub_group(sub_group_id, timer_names)
@@ -2975,17 +3086,40 @@ def dump_post_step_gradients(self):
                 print(f'Post-Step Norms {i} {param_id} = {norm_list}')
 
     @instrument_w_nvtx
-    def unscale_and_clip_grads(self, sub_group_id, total_norm):
+    def _combined_grad_scale(self, total_norm):
         # compute combined scale factor for this group
         combined_scale = self.loss_scale
         if self.clip_grad > 0.:
             # norm is in fact norm*scale
             clip = ((total_norm / self.loss_scale) + 1e-6) / self.clip_grad
             clip = torch.clamp(clip, min=1.0)
             combined_scale = clip * self.loss_scale
+        return combined_scale
 
+    def unscale_and_clip_grads(self, sub_group_id, total_norm):
+        combined_scale = self._combined_grad_scale(total_norm)
         self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].grad.mul_(1. / combined_scale)
 
+    def _grad_scale_for_cpu_adam(self, sub_group_id, total_norm):
+        """The factor unscale_and_clip_grads would multiply this sub-group's gradients by, when DeepSpeedCPUAdam can
+        apply it while loading each gradient instead; None otherwise.

+        return float(1. / self._combined_grad_scale(total_norm))

issue_comments.body:
Hi @pengdurice,

It's great to see this PR addressing CPU optimizer overhead, as it closely aligns with our work on ReplayOpt and ReFlow (#8719).

Our research focuses on the memory bandwidth bottlenecks of CPU-offloaded optimizers. In ReplayOpt, accepted to IEEE Computer Architecture Letters (CAL), we explored reducing the critical-path overhead of optimizer-state updates. Building on this work, ReFlow further reduces memory traffic through register-resident SIMD fusion and overlaps CPU optimizer execution with GPU computation through decoupled scheduling.

In particular, ReFlow already implements the two main optimizations in this PR: fusing gradient scaling/clipping into CPU SIMD kernels and directly generating FP16/BF16 parameters without a separate conversion pass.

There are also opportunities for further optimization. For configurations using BF16 gradient accumulation, or without gradient accumulation, gradients can be transferred to the CPU in BF16 and promoted to FP32 only within SIMD registers during the optimizer update. This reduces not only PCIe traffic but also gradient-related CPU memory traffic, which is especially beneficial for memory-bandwidth-bound CPU optimizers. The in-register conversion is relatively inexpensive and avoids a separate FP32 conversion pass.

With these optimizations and asynchronous scheduling, ReFlow achieves up to 4.0× higher training throughput than ZeRO-Infinity on a single B200 and 1.86× on four B200 GPUs.

I originally implemented these optimizations in separate ReFlow kernels to minimize regression risks and preserve the stability of the existing DeepSpeed CPU optimizer path. However, since this PR is addressing the same underlying bottlenecks, I think this could be a good opportunity to incorporate ReFlow's non-asynchronous optimizations into the default CPU-offload path, while keeping asynchronous execution optional.

Would you be willing to review my PR (#8719) and share your thoughts on this direction? I'd greatly appreciate your feedback and would be happy to help with the integration and validation.

The ReFlow paper has also been accepted to ASPLOS 2027 and is expected to be publicly available soon. I'd be happy to share a copy directly if it would help with reviewing the design and evaluation.

Thank you for your time and consideration!

reviews.body:
Thanks for this. Most of it checks out: the clip factor comes from the same folding-aware `scaled_global_grad_norm` (partition group → MP reduce → `_autoep_expert_parallel_group`), overflow returns before the sub-group loop, `IncrementStep` is idempotent across pieces, pieces are aligned to `SIMD_WIDTH*8`, and the bf16 store is RNE with NaN→0x7fc0 like torch. The new kernel tests pass bitwise on AVX-512 for me. Small thing: the first commit is #8840's head, so "Builds on #TODO" should read #8840.

One blocking issue and a few should-fix items below.

**1. [blocking] Params with no gradient this step diverge from the unfused path** — [`stage3.py:3022-3024`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/5f663c08e5ad46d0088e379c55a8b900633e6360/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L3022-L3024)

Skipping the in-place `unscale_and_clip_grads` has two side effects:

- In offload mode a sub-group's fp32 grad buffer isn't zeroed between steps, and `_finalize_offload_gradient_accumulation` only refreshes params reduced in this window. On master, `unscale_and_clip_grads` rescales that stale region in place every step; on the fused path it keeps its raw loss-scaled, unclipped value and is only multiplied by the current factor. Repro on the CPU accelerator (1 rank, fp32 model, `offload_optimizer: {device: cpu, pin_memory: false}`, `gradient_clipping: 1e-3`, a layer used only on step 0, 3 steps): every parameter is bitwise equal between the fused and unfused paths except the unused layer, which differs by up to 5.9e-3. Under AutoEP this is any expert that receives no tokens in a step.
- After `step()`, `safe_get_full_grad` now returns unscaled, unclipped grads (0.221 vs 2.97e-4 in the same repro).

Options: take the fused path only when every param of the sub-group was reduced this window (e.g. check against `_offload_boundary_param_ids`), or zero the non-reduced regions in `_finalize_offload_gradient_accumulation`. The second would also fix an existing master issue where those stale grads are applied by the step but left out of the norm. Either way, a regression test with a conditionally-unused layer would lock it in.

**2. [should-fix] Scope is wider than the description** — [`stage3.py:3103`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/5f663c08e5ad46d0088e379c55a8b900633e6360/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L3103)

The description says fp16 and `pin_memory: false` keep the current path, but `_grad_scale_for_cpu_adam` has no dtype or pin gate: DeepSpeed's own fp16 (dynamic loss scale) and `pin_memory: false` both take the fused grad-scale path (the repro above is `pin_memory: false`). Only the copy-back half is bf16 + pinned. Could you either gate it, or update the description and add an fp16 case with a forced overflow showing the step and the loss-scale update are skipped and nothing is written?

**3. [should-fix] `step_pieces` bypasses `Optimizer.step`** — [`cpu_adam.py:194`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/5f663c08e5ad46d0088e379c55a8b900633e6360/deepspeed/ops/adam/cpu_adam.py#L194)

It doesn't go through torch's wrapped `Optimizer.step`, so step pre/post hooks don't run, the profiler loses the `Optimizer.step#DeepSpeedCPUAdam.step` range, and `_opt_called` is never set. A torch LR scheduler built on the basic optimizer then warns that `lr_scheduler.step()` was called before `optimizer.step()`, and with ratio 1.0 + bf16 + pinned `optimizer.step()` is never called at all. Could this go through a `step(..., pieces=...)` overload, or run the hooks and mark the step manually?

**4. [should-fix] Copy-back test fails on the CPU accelerator** — [`test_zero.py:2098`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/5f663c08e5ad46d0088e379c55a8b900633e6360/tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py#L2098)

With 2 CPU ranks the destination is never on a device, so `assert calls, "no sub-group took the fused copy-back path"` fails. It needs a skip when `get_accelerator().device_name() == "cpu"` (same issue as in #8840). `TestZero3CpuAdamGradScale` is fine on CPU.

**5. [question] ARM** — [`cpu_adam_impl.cpp:274`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/5f663c08e5ad46d0088e379c55a8b900633e6360/csrc/adam/cpu_adam_impl.cpp#L274)

On SVE builds (Grace) `adam_copy_supported()` is false, so only the grad-scale half runs, via the new `svmul_f32_x`. The description lists ARM as unvalidated. I have a GH200 and can run `test_cpu_adam_grad_scale_matches_scaling_in_place` and `test_cpu_adam_step_pieces_matches_step` there if that helps.

**6. [nit]** `src.is_pinned()` here vs `accelerator.is_pinned(src)` in #8840, and the staging allocation duplicates `_copy_through_pinned_staging`; a shared helper would keep them in sync. Also `_optimizer_step(..., grad_scale=...)` is now always passed by keyword while SuperOffload's override keeps the old signature. That's safe today only because SuperOffload overrides `step()`; passing it only when not `None` would be more robust.
